findings.explanation: high confidence.  Witness: The wild inertia group of the local field $K_{\infty,w} \cong \mathbb{F}_v^{(p)}((t))$ is a non-trivial (in fact infinite) pro-$p$ group, so by Artin-Schreier theory $H^1(K_{\infty,w}, \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}) = K_{\infty,w}/\wp(K_{\infty,w}) \neq 0$. Thus the absolute Galois group of $K_{\infty,w}$ is not isomorphic to $\prod_{\ell \neq p} \mathbb{Z}_\ell$. Accordingly, the claim that $\ker f_4 = \operatorname{coker} f_4 = 0$ based on this prime-to-$p$ assertion is unjustified and mathematically incorrect.

evidence.text: As \( K_\infty \) is unramified at every prime \( v \), we obtain that for any prime \( v \) and \( w \mid v \), \( \operatorname{Gal}(K_{\infty,w}/K_{\infty,w}) \cong \prod_{\ell \neq p} \mathbb{Z}_\ell \). Therefore, \( \ker f_4 = \operatorname{coker} f_4 = 0 \).

findings.explanation:
high confidence.  Witness: The absolute Galois group $G_{K_{\mathrm{cyc}, w}}$ of the local field $K_{\mathrm{cyc}, w}$ has tame inertia quotient isomorphic to $\prod_{r 
eq p} \mathbb{Z}_r$. Since $\ell 
eq p$, this quotient contains $\mathbb{Z}_\ell$, so $G_{K_{\mathrm{cyc}, w}}$ has non-trivial continuous homomorphisms to $\mathbb{Z}/\ell\mathbb{Z}$, hence $\ker g_3$ is non-trivial in general rather than trivial as claimed based on $G_{K_{\mathrm{cyc}, w}} \cong \prod_{r 
eq \ell} \mathbb{Z}_r$. In particular, the local Galois group is not of order prime to $\ell$. Consequently, $\ker g_3$ and $\operatorname{coker} g_3$ need not be trivial and the local terms in the Euler characteristic do not vanish for this reason without taking tame inertia into account (as was done in Case 2 via local Euler-Poincaré characteristics). In fact, the same mistake appears earlier in [p21-0], where the authors write $\operatorname{Gal}(K_{\infty,w}/K_{\infty,w}) \cong \prod_{\ell 
eq p} \mathbb{Z}_\ell$ and deduce $\ker f_4 = \operatorname{coker} f_4 = 0$. In [p24-6], asserting that the absolute Galois group is $\prod_{r 
eq \ell} \mathbb{Z}_r$ completely ignores the inertia group (specifically tame inertia, which contains $\mathbb{Z}_\ell$ since $\ell 
eq p$), and the subsequent deduction that $\ker g_3$ and $\operatorname{coker} g_3$ are trivial is mathematically invalid for this reason. Hence the proof given in [p24-6] fails due to this false claim about the local Galois group and the resulting vanishing of $\ker g_3$ and $\operatorname{coker} g_3$. The claim correctly identifies this fatal error in the proof of Theorem A.1 in [p24-6]. Thus there is a confirmed error in [p24-6]. In [p24-6]: 'As K_cyc is unramified at every prime v, we obtain that for any prime v and w | v, Gal(K_cyc,w/K_cyc,w) ≅ ∏_{r≠ℓ} Z_r. Therefore, ker g₃ and coker g₃ are trivial.' All criteria are met. Confirming error as requested.

evidence.text:
Since, E₁ and E₂ are non-isotrivial, hence we get that E₁[ℓ^∞](K_cyc) and E₂[ℓ^∞](K_cyc) are finite ([BL09b, Lemma 3.2]). Hence, ker(g₂) and coker(g₂) are finite.
As K_cyc is unramified at every prime v, we obtain that for any prime v and w | v, Gal(K_cyc,w/K_cyc,w) ≅ ∏_{r≠ℓ} Z_r. Therefore, ker g₃ and coker g₃ are trivial.
